summary.text: Jack Reed is the Democratic incumbent seeking a sixth term in the U.S. Senate. A Cranston native and West Point graduate, he served as an Army officer, practiced banking and securities law, and served in the Rhode Island State Senate and the U.S. House before being elected to the Senate in 1996. He is the ranking member of the Senate Armed Services Committee.

paragraphs.text: Born and raised in Cranston, Rhode Island, according to his Senate office; his father was a World War II veteran and school custodial supervisor and his mother a homemaker. Ballotpedia lists his birthplace as Providence, in 1949.
Attended St. Matthew's Elementary School and graduated from La Salle Academy in Providence.
Graduated from the U.S. Military Academy at West Point in 1971, earned a master's degree in public policy from Harvard's Kennedy School in 1973, and a J.D. from Harvard Law School in 1982.

Served in the 82nd Airborne Division as an infantry platoon leader, company commander and battalion staff officer, then taught economics and international relations at West Point as an associate professor. He left active duty as a captain in 1979 and served in the Army Reserves until 1991, leaving as a major.
Practiced law after law school, first at Sutherland, Asbill & Brennan and then at Edwards & Angell in Providence, specializing in banking and securities law and doing pro bono work for Amos House.
Served three terms in the Rhode Island State Senate (1985-1991).
Elected to the U.S. House of Representatives in 1990 and served three terms from 1991 to 1997, representing Rhode Island's 2nd District.
Elected to the U.S. Senate in 1996 to succeed Claiborne Pell and has served since 1997. He is ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and a senior member of the Appropriations Committee.

According to his Senate office, he was part of the bipartisan group that drafted the CARES Act and wrote provisions of the 2010 Wall Street reform law; he and his wife, Julia Hart Reed, have a daughter, Emily.
